metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the exact AST match shape (e.g. an `ast.Attribute` whose value is any expression resolving to the section — a `<section>.<field>` attribute-chain tail, independent of the base being `cfg` / `load_config()` / an aliased-module call / a section-object local), and state how each dataclass field is mapped to its section (via `_SECTIONS`/`_SECTION_CLASSES`).
evidence: config.py:422 `return load_config().mcp.readonly` (base is a call, not `cfg`)
_mcp_auth.py:645-650 / mcp_server.py:527 read via section-object locals `mcp_cfg.auth_introspection_endpoint`, `mcp_cfg.http_allowed_hosts` — section name absent at the read site
Fields are dataclass attributes; the (section↔field) mapping lives in `_SECTIONS`/`_SECTION_CLASSES`, so the checker must also map each field to its section to know the pattern
findings.finding: The plan specifies the read pattern literally as `cfg.<section>.<field>`, but actual read sites in src/ rarely start with a bare `cfg` name — they root at a call (`load_config().mcp.readonly`, `load_config().reconciler.max_acting_fraction`), a call on an arbitrary alias (`config.load_config(repo_root).verify.overlap_enabled`), or a section object bound to a local (`mcp_cfg.auth_introspection_endpoint`). The plan does not state the exact AST shape the check matches, and that shape is decisive: matching the literal 3-part chain FPs across most of the surface, while relaxing it invites the leaf-collision failure below.
scenarios: Checker walks src/ for `verify.overlap_enabled` but the only read is `load_config().verify.overlap_enabled` on an aliased module — matched only if the check keys on the `.section.field` tail regardless of the base expression
mcp/reconciler sections read exclusively through section-object locals (`mcp_cfg.<field>`) — invisible to any pattern that requires the section name at the read site
findings.suggested_fix: Match on the `.<section>.<field>` attribute-chain tail (base-expression-agnostic) AND additionally recognize section-object-bound reads (`<local>.<field>` where `<local>` is annotated/assigned as the section type, e.g. `mcp_cfg: McpConfig`), rather than requiring a literal `cfg` root.

findings.finding: The `cfg.<section>.<field>` two-segment attribute-chain match will false-flag live, genuinely-read fields whose reads go through a bound section object or getattr, contradicting the plan's 'zero-reference-only / refactors cannot FP' guarantee.
findings.location: Approach ('require >=1 attribute-read site (cfg.<section>.<field>)'); Acceptance Criteria line 3 ('Zero-reference-only firing')
findings.suggested_fix: Have the walk track local names bound to a `.<section>` attribute (and section-typed parameters) and count `<local>.<field>` reads against that section; treat `getattr(<section-obj>, '<field>')` string literals as reads too.

findings.finding: The read-site detection pattern 'cfg.<section>.<field>' assumes a fixed receiver identifier ('cfg'), but the plan does not state how the AST walk identifies a read when the config object is bound to a different name (self.config, settings, an aliased import, or passed as a parameter). An AST attribute-read match keyed only on the literal 'cfg' prefix would miss legitimate reads under other receiver names and FP-fire on genuinely-read fields.
findings.suggested_fix: State the match rule: detect any attribute-access chain ending in `.<section>.<field>` for known section/field pairs, independent of the base identifier, OR enumerate the accepted config receiver names.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate reads by section (require the section context — attribute chain or section-typed base — not a bare `.<field>` leaf) so a same-named unrelated local cannot satisfy a field's read requirement.
evidence: classify.py:308/324/334 and binding_walk.py:105/241 read a PLAIN parameter `max_acting_fraction`, unrelated to `cfg.reconciler.max_acting_fraction`
`threshold` is a field on both TicketClarityConfig and CompactConfig; `dir` is TrackerConfig.dir — generic names likely to appear as unrelated locals
findings.finding: If the check relaxes to match only the trailing `.<field>` attribute name (to tolerate the varied base expressions above), it becomes a proxy: a config field passes on a name-collision with an unrelated local/parameter of the same name, even when the config value is never read. `reconciler.max_acting_fraction` is the concrete case — its value is read once then flows through a plain parameter `max_acting_fraction` read throughout classify.py/binding_walk.py; generic leaf names like `dir` (tracker) and `threshold` (ticket_clarity, compact) collide similarly.
scenarios: A future field is added to the schema but never wired; a same-named local elsewhere in src/ makes the gate pass, so the inert knob ships undetected

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate (or define by path/glob) exactly which modules constitute 'schema/config plumbing' and are excluded from read-site counting.
evidence: Plan says 'outside the schema/config plumbing modules' but never lists which files/modules constitute plumbing
A read inside a plumbing module counting (or not counting) determines whether the gate fires — this is load-bearing for correctness
findings.finding: The set of 'schema/config plumbing modules' that are excluded from read-site counting is not enumerated, yet the AST walk must define exactly which modules don't count as legitimate read sites.
findings.location: Approach: 'require >=1 attribute-read site (cfg.<section>.<field>) outside the schema/config plumbing modules'
scenarios: A field read only inside a config-serialization helper: does that count as a read or is that module excluded?
Executor must guess the exclusion set, producing either false passes (plumbing reads counted) or churn
findings.suggested_fix: State the exclusion set explicitly, e.g. 'reads inside src/rebar/**/_config_schema.py and the named config-loader module(s) are excluded; all other src/rebar modules count', and make it a small configurable list in the check.

findings.finding: The plan does not name the set of modules that constitute 'schema/config plumbing' (the excluded read sites). Without an enumerated exclusion list, an executor cannot deterministically decide which files are ignored when counting read sites.
findings.suggested_fix: List the excluded paths explicitly, e.g. `src/rebar/**/_config_schema.py` and the config-loader module(s), as a constant in the check script.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-scope the read-via marker enumeration to include getattr-dispatched fields (mcp.readonly / allow_llm / allow_jira_sync) and confirm the plumbing exclusion does not strand a field whose sole literal read is the config.py shared resolver (e.g. exempt such single-resolver reads or treat them as valid read sites).
evidence: mcp_server.py:414 `return getattr(rebar.config.load_config().mcp, attr)` — `allow_llm`/`allow_jira_sync` read only via this dispatch (mcp_server.py:428-430)
No literal `.allow_llm` config attribute read exists in src/ (search: only `ctx.allow_llm` context-callable sites, not the config field)
config.py:422 `load_config().mcp.readonly` is the sole literal read of `readonly`, but sits in the excluded config plumbing module
findings.finding: The plan estimates read-via markers as 'expected small', but the codebase shows several fields whose ONLY non-plumbing read is indirect and will each require a marker: `mcp.allow_llm` and `mcp.allow_jira_sync` are read in src/ solely via `getattr(load_config().mcp, attr)` in `_mcp_gate`, and `mcp.readonly`'s single literal read `load_config().mcp.readonly` lives inside config.py — which the plan excludes as 'config plumbing' — leaving its only non-excluded read as the same getattr dispatch. The plan should also confirm the plumbing exclusion doesn't strand a field whose sole literal read is the shared resolver in config.py.
findings.location: Scope — "'# read-via:' markers ... expected small" + Approach plumbing exclusion
scenarios: At implementation, the whole gated-mcp set (readonly, allow_llm, allow_jira_sync) plus section-object-bound mcp/reconciler fields require read-via markers, exceeding the 'small' estimate
A field whose only real read is the config.py shared resolver is forced to carry a marker purely because of the plumbing exclusion

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the new check reuses/extends the existing AST scaffolding (scripts/gen_env_registry.py) and mirrors the established justified-exemption pattern (EXCLUDED_JOBS-style), or justify why a separate walker is warranted.
evidence: Plan: 'Env vars are already covered by the docs/env-vars.md drift gate; schema fields have no equivalent.'

Prior art in-repo: scripts/gen_env_registry.py already implements an AST walk over src/rebar with a scan() collecting per-name read sites and a KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS shim-resolution table plus explicit unioning of indirect reads (aliases, derived MCP vars).

Prior art in-repo: scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py implements a drift gate with an EXCLUDED_JOBS escape list requiring a one-line justification — the same escape-with-pointer shape as the plan's '# read-via:' marker.
The plan references these gates only by analogy ('alongside existing gates') and does not state whether it extends the existing AST scaffolding or writes a new independent walker.
findings.finding: The plan cites the docs/env-vars.md drift gate as the env-var analog but does not commit to reusing the repo's existing AST-gate scaffolding (scripts/gen_env_registry.py) or its established justified-exemption pattern, risking a parallel reimplementation of an already-proven walker.
findings.location: Approach / Scope ('new check script (AST walk over src/rebar) + CI wiring')
scenarios: Executor writes a second, subtly-different AST walker whose module-discovery/exclusion rules diverge from gen_env_registry.py, so the two gates disagree about what 'src/rebar' scope means.
The proven pattern for indirect reads (unioning alias/derived surface) in gen_env_registry.py is not carried over, so the new check's '# read-via:' handling reinvents that logic inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Prior art' note committing to reuse gen_env_registry.py's AST scan (or its module-discovery helpers) and to model the '# read-via:' marker on the existing EXCLUDED_JOBS/KNOWN_ENV_HELPERS justified-exemption convention, so both config gates share one scoping definition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how each schema field's (section, field) pair and its read-pattern (attribute chain, and whether subscript access counts) is derived for the AST match.
evidence: The check needs to know each field's owning section to construct the cfg.<section>.<field> attribute chain to match
Plan asserts the pattern shape but not the field→section derivation
findings.finding: The plan does not specify how a schema field is mapped to its cfg.<section>.<field> read pattern (how the check derives the section name and field name to grep/AST-match for each field).
findings.location: Approach: 'for each field in _config_schema.py, require >=1 attribute-read site (cfg.<section>.<field>)'
scenarios: A field whose section is determined by class/dataclass nesting — executor must decide how to reconstruct the full attribute path
Aliased or renamed access (cfg['section']['field'] subscript vs attribute) not addressed
